For the maximum: \(x \le \min(1820,1651,1182)=1182\), and this is achievable by setting 1182 houses to have all three, 272 to have dog+cat only, 366 to have dog only, and 197 to have cat only. Thus \(x=1182\).

For the minimum: use complements.
\[
|\text{no dog}|=2017-1820=197,\quad
|\text{no cat}|=2017-1651=366,\quad
|\text{no turtle}|=2017-1182=835.
\]
To minimize the triple intersection, maximize the union of these complements, at most
\[
197+366+835=1398.
\]
So
\[
y \ge 2017-1398=619.
\]
This is achievable by making the complement sets disjoint, so \(y=619\).

Therefore,
\[
x-y=1182-619=563.
\]
\[
\boxed{563}
\]
